{{Otheruses|Chaos|more=Hell (disambiguation)|more2=Void (disambiguation)}}
{{Quote|Similarly, Chaos is where dead Sith Lords are believed to dwell in torment.|Darth Plagueis|<ref name="Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side">''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Markaragnos23.jpg|thumb|right|120px|The spirit of [[Marka Ragnos]]]]
'''Chaos''', referred to as '''Hell''' in [[Corellian/Legends|Corellian]] mythology<ref name="ESB">{{Film|V}}</ref> and also known as '''The Void''',<ref name="DESB">''[[Dark Empire Sourcebook]]''</ref> was a reputedly dark<ref name="TNMS">{{SW|url=news/the-not-so-magnificent-seven|text=The Not-So Magnificent Seven|int=The Not-So Magnificent Seven|nolive=1}}</ref> realm<ref name="END">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/insideronline/88/indexp2.html|text=''Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties''|int=Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties}}</ref> that the [[Force ghost/Legends|spirits]] of deceased [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lords of the Sith]] were believed to inhabit instead of the [[Netherworld of the Force/Legends|Netherworld of the Force]].<ref name="Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side" /> In [[Naboo (people)/Legends|Naboo]] [[Naboo religion|mythology]], Chaos was envisioned as a dark pit kept closed by six impenetrable gates.<ref name="Darth P">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref>

==History==
{{Quote|But this old man called my spirit back from Chaos...|Freedon Nadd|<ref name="FNU1">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Freedon Nadd Uprising 1|''Tales of the Jedi – The Freedon Nadd Uprising'' 1]]</ref>}}
[[Ommin/Legends|Ommin]] summoned the spirit of [[Freedon Nadd]] from Chaos during the [[Freedon Nadd Uprising]].<ref name="FNU1" /> The [[Dark Underlord]] was said to have been summoned from Chaos by a [[Sith acolyte/Legends|Sith Acolyte]] during the [[New Sith Wars]].<ref name="END" /> [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] feared that his soul would fall into Chaos following his [[Battle of Onderon (Galactic Civil War)|final death]], where he would be a wandering, disembodied spirit residing in perpetual madness.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Characters">''[[The Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref> Palpatine convinced [[Arden Lyn]] to become an [[Emperor's Hand/Legends|Emperor's Hand]] by promising to summon [[Xendor]]'s spirit from Chaos.<ref name="tep">{{GamerCite|5|The Emperor's Pawns}}</ref> [[Marka Ragnos]]'s spirit was summoned from Chaos<ref name="END" /> by [[Tavion Axmis]] and the [[Disciples of Ragnos]], though Ragnos was summarily [[Battle of Korriban (Disciples of Ragnos crisis)|defeated]] by [[Jaden Korr]].<ref name="Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy]]''</ref> It was believed that if a [[The Force/Legends|Force]] user's body perished after a failed attempt at [[essence transfer]], the user's life energy was lost and dispersed in Chaos.<ref name="DESB" /> [[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Darth Plagueis]] once reported that, according to legend, those who failed to punish their enemies during their lifetime would be forced to harbor their ill feelings in Chaos forever. Plagueis, however, didn't believe Chaos was a real place, but only the perception of imminent dissolution some beings felt when they died. In his opinion, only stronger minds who refused the loss of their identity would perceive this pain.<ref name="Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side" /> Chaos was also briefly referenced by [[House Palpatine/Legends|House Palpatine]] Patriarch [[Cosinga Palpatine]], citing that House Palpatine was one of the six gates that "hold back Chaos."<ref name="Darth P" /> Chaos was not inescapable, however: Palpatine, after perishing during the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], had escaped Chaos with the help of the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lords of the Sith]] in the [[Great Temple (Korriban)|Great Temple]] of [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]],<ref name="EE 2">[[Empire's End 2|''Empire's End'' 2]]</ref> [[Jeng Droga]], and [[Sate Pestage/Legends|Sate Pestage]],<ref name="tep" /> and required several deceased Jedi to ensure he never escaped again after his [[Battle of Onderon (Galactic Civil War)|final death]] on [[Onderon]].<ref name="EE 2" />

==Chaos in language==
{{Quote|Chaos take your mission!|[[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], to [[Raymus Antilles/Legends|Raymus Antilles]]|<ref name="Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope (novel)">[[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope'' novelization]]</ref>}}
"Chaos take me" was a mild expletive, sometimes used when one decided to do something he or she knew was not very wise.<ref name="Lando Calrissian and the Mindharp of Sharu">''[[Lando Calrissian and the Mindharp of Sharu]]''</ref> Saying "Go to Hell" or "See you in Hell"<ref name="ESB" /> were similar expletives meant to insult or threaten whomever they were directed to. Another use was in the phrase "There will be Hell to pay."<ref name="Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope">{{Film|IV}}</ref> They can also be used when either startled or expressing disbelief regarding someone's story, evidenced by the phrases "What the hell is that?" and "Like hell you did!," respectively.<ref name="Rookies">{{TCW|Rookies (episode)}}</ref> A similar phrase, "Where the hell are you going?!," can be used in the context of the former.<ref name="Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope" /> A more toned-down version of the expletive is known as "Heck."<ref name="Millennium Falcon">[[Millennium Falcon (novel)|''Millennium Falcon'']]</ref>

Beings destined for hell were considered "damned."<ref name="Star Wars 6: Is This the Final Chapter?">[[Star Wars (1977) 6|''Star Wars'' (1977) 6]]</ref> The word "damn" is also sometimes used as an expletive, either for emphasis (eg, when describing how good someone is at their profession)<ref name="Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones">{{Film|II}}</ref> or to curse someone.<ref name="Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]''</ref>

[[Don-Wan Kihotay]] used the term ''hell-spawned'' to refer to [[Demon/Legends|demonic]] things like the [[Behemoth from the World Below]]'s fin bolts.<ref name="Star Wars 10: Behemoth from the World Below">[[Star Wars (1977) 10|''Star Wars'' (1977) 10]]</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
''Hell'' was used twice as an expletive in the [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars|''Clone Wars'']] episode "[[Rookies (episode)|Rookies]]" during its initial airings, although it was censored in subsequent reairings. By 2021, however, the original was restored.<ref name="Rookies" />

In [[Wikipedia:Greek mythology|Greek mythology]], ''[[Wikipedia:Chaos|Chaos]]'' refers to [[Wikipedia:Tartarus|Tartarus]], the Greek version of Hell. It also refers to the primeval emptiness of the universe before things came into being.<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://www.britannica.com/topic/Chaos-ancient-Greek-religion|text=Chaos|quote='''Chaos''', (Greek: "Abyss") in early Greek cosmology, either the primeval emptiness of the universe before things came into being or the abyss of Tartarus, the underworld.|archivedate=20201124051557}}</ref>
